info.title: OrbitID API
info.summary: Authentication, users, organizations, webhooks and OIDC for a self-hosted OrbitID instance.
info.description:
OrbitID exposes three surfaces on one origin.

- **Frontend API** (`/v1/client/*`): for browsers. Authenticated by the httpOnly `__client` cookie, which is
  created on first use. Never call it with a secret key.
- **Backend API** (`/v1/*`): for your servers. Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer sk_...` with the
  instance secret key. Responses include `private_metadata`.
- **OAuth/OIDC provider** (`/oauth/*`, `/.well-known/*`): standard endpoints for third-party clients.

All JSON is snake_case, all timestamps are Unix epoch **milliseconds**, and every id is prefixed with its
object type (`user_...`, `sess_...`, `org_...`). Errors use the envelope described by the `ApiError` schema,
except on the OAuth protocol endpoints, which answer with the standard `{ error, error_description }` shape.
List endpoints on the Backend API return `{ data, total_count }` and accept `limit`, `offset` and `order_by`.

Rate-limited endpoints answer `429` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. Sensitive flows (sign-in,
sign-up, code verification, session-token minting) are limited per IP and per identifier.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: Dashboard sign-in: accounts with the Owner or Administrator role open a revocable httpOnly console session. The secret key does not open the dashboard.

get.description: Answers 200 when the process is up, with the publishable key and the database in use so a client can check that it is talking to the instance it expects. Intended for load balancers and container health checks.

Reports whether this browser still has a live console session. Used on dashboard load so an expired or revoked cookie sends the operator to the sign-in screen. Answers `401` and clears the cookie when there is none. Requests with a live console cookie are not charged; others share the status check's budget of 120 requests a minute per address (the instance's rate limiting setting turns it off); over budget it answers `429` with `Retry-After`.

delete.description: Revokes this browser's operator session and clears the cookie. A console opened from an account also ends that account's session on this browser. Safe to call without a session. A sign-out that ends a session is never charged; one that finds nothing to end (no cookies, or cookies that match nothing) is rate limited to 30 requests a minute per address (the instance's rate limiting setting turns it off); over budget it answers `429` with `Retry-After`.

204.description: The session is revoked and the cookie cleared.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: `true` also signs this browser's account out when no console session is linked to it. A console opened from an account always signs that account out.

get.description: The dashboard's single boot request: the live console session, the account signed in on this browser and whether it may open the console, and whether the instance still needs its owner. Never answers `401`; signed out is a normal answer. Refused from any origin other than this instance's own. Requests with a live console cookie are not charged; others are rate limited to 120 requests a minute per address (the instance's rate limiting setting turns it off); over budget it answers `429` with `Retry-After`.

post.description: Only while the instance has no account. Creates the account with the `app:sys_owner` role, signs it in on this browser (the `__client` cookie) and opens the console (the `__orbit_operator` cookie), atomically: of two concurrent requests exactly one succeeds. Answers `403` once any account exists or the instance has ever been claimed (an owner was created, or the instance predates owners); such an instance grants the Owner role with `orbitid owner <email>` instead. The password must satisfy the instance's password policy. Rate limited to 10 attempts per 10 minutes per address (the instance's rate limiting setting turns it off); over budget it answers `429` with `Retry-After`.

201.description: The owner is created, signed in and in the console.

post.summary: Open the console from a signed-in account
post.description: Opens the console for the account signed in on this browser (its `__client` cookie only; a session token sent as a bearer is ignored), when one of its instance roles grants `app:sys_dashboard:access` (the seeded Owner and Administrator roles do). The console session is tied to that account session and is re-checked on every request: removing the role, banning the account or ending its session ends the console for good. Rate limited to 20 requests a minute per address (the instance's rate limiting setting turns it off); over budget it answers `429` with `Retry-After`.

201.description: Sets the `__orbit_operator` cookie and answers with the status: the new console session and the account it belongs to.

get.description: Public projection of the instance settings that every UI component renders from: enabled factors, attribute requirements, organization settings and branding. Cacheable for 60 seconds; contains no secrets.

post.description: Creates a sign-in attempt for this client and advances it as far as the request allows. `status` says what is needed next: `needs_identifier`, `needs_first_factor`, `needs_second_factor`, `needs_new_password` or `complete` (with `created_session_id`). Starting an OAuth or enterprise SSO strategy returns `first_factor_verification.external_verification_redirect_url`; navigate the browser there. Failed password attempts count towards the user's lockout, and unknown identifiers return `form_identifier_not_found` unless enumeration protection is on. Rate limited per IP and identifier.

identifier.description: Email address, phone number or username. Required unless `strategy` is `oauth_*`, `enterprise_sso` or `ticket`.

strategy.description: First-factor strategy to start with: `password`, `email_code`, `email_link`, `phone_code`, `passkey`, `ticket`, `enterprise_sso` or `oauth_<provider>`.

ticket.description: Invitation ticket for sign-up. Tickets cannot replace authentication during sign-in; actor and operator-minted sign-in tokens are not accepted.

transfer.description: Carry a transferable OAuth verification from a sign-in into this sign-up.

get.description: Lets a second tab or a polling page observe progress (for example after an email link was opened elsewhere).

post.description: Sends the email code, magic link or SMS code for the chosen strategy, or arms an OAuth redirect. The response carries the updated sign-in, so read `first_factor_verification` for the strategy state.
Verifies the password, code, passkey assertion or OAuth callback. Wrong codes and passwords return `form_code_incorrect` / `form_password_incorrect` and count towards the lockout. Rate limited.

signature.description: Signed message for a web3 strategy.

post.description: Sends an SMS code when the strategy is `phone_code`; `totp` and `backup_code` need no preparation.

post.summary: Set a new password during sign-in
post.description: Completes the `needs_new_password` state, which is entered after a password-reset code was verified. The password policy is enforced. `sign_out_of_other_sessions` ends the user's other active sessions.

Creates an account attempt. The response's `missing_fields` and `unverified_fields` are computed from the instance's attribute settings; fill them in with `PATCH` and verify identifiers with `prepare_verification`/`attempt_verification`. Sign-up completes (`status: complete`, `created_session_id` set) as soon as nothing is missing. Sign-up is gated by the instance's sign-up mode, the allow/block lists and invitation tickets. Rate limited per IP.

get.summary: Refresh a session token during a page navigation
get.description: Used by the Next.js middleware. When a hard navigation arrives with an expired `__session` cookie but a live `__client` cookie, the app redirects the browser here with `redirect_url`. The server answers `302` to `redirect_url` with `__orbit_handshake=<session token>`, or `__orbit_handshake=signed_out` when there is no active session. `redirect_url` must be an allowed origin. The response is not cacheable and sends no referrer. See docs/HANDSHAKE.md.

parameters.description: Where to send the browser next.

post.description: The signed-in user approves or denies the device that showed `user_code`. A code that expired answers 410; one already decided answers 409.

signing_key.description: Verification key for templates with a custom signing key: an HS256 secret or a public JWK.

secret.description: Base32 secret, returned once during setup.

qr_code.description: `data:` URL of a QR code for the URI.

identification_requirements.description: One entry per accepted identifier combination.

social.description: Enabled social providers keyed by provider name.

version.description: The running server version and the last release check. The check asks GitHub every 6 hours unless ORBITID_UPDATE_CHECK=false; this response only reads the cached answer.

update_check.description: Whether this server checks for new releases.

latest.description: The newest published release, once a check has succeeded.

update_available.description: True when `latest` is newer than `current` by semver precedence.

checked_at.description: When `latest` was last confirmed, in milliseconds since the epoch.

defaultRole.description: The `app:` role every non-guest user without an explicit instance-role assignment holds. `null` grants nothing. System (`app:sys_*`) and `org:` keys are refused.

Instance.description: Instance settings. Secret values (`smtpUrl`, `twilioAuthToken`, `captchaSecret`, social `clientSecret`) are returned as `••••` together with a sibling `<field>Set` boolean; send the tree back without the masked values to keep the stored secrets.

items.description: JSON Web Key. RSA keys carry `n`/`e`; EC keys carry `x`/`y`/`crv`.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

UserInfo.description: Claims for the user behind the access token: `sub`, and whichever of `email`, `email_verified`, `name`, `given_name`, `family_name`, `preferred_username`, `picture`, `locale`, `updated_at`, `phone_number`, `phone_number_verified`, `groups`, `org_*` and `organizations` the scopes allow.

message.description: Short human-readable message, safe to show to the end user.

long_message.description: Longer explanation with the fix, when there is one.

errors.description: One entry per problem; a single request can report several validation errors.

trace_id.description: Correlation id for the request. Include it when reporting a problem.

operator_session.description: The live console session on this browser, if any.

console_access.description: One of the account's instance roles grants `app:sys_dashboard:access`.

user.description: The account signed in to this instance on this browser (its own `__client` session), if any.

setup_required.description: The instance has no account yet. The first person to finish `POST /v1/operator_sessions/setup` becomes its owner.

console_unclaimed.description: Accounts exist but none can open the console (an instance from before owners). Whoever runs the server grants the Owner role with `orbitid owner <email>`.

OperatorStatus.description: Everything the dashboard needs to choose its first screen, in one answer.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be read: malformed JSON, an unparsable body or an invalid query parameter.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid credentials. The Frontend API also answers this when the client cookie is gone.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed. The Frontend API also returns this for a pending session that still has to enrol a second factor (`session_pending`), and for missing organization permissions.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or it belongs to someone else.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with existing state: a duplicate record, an already accepted invitation, or the last admin.

UnprocessableEntity.description: Validation failed on the request body or query. `meta.param_name` names the offending field.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limited. `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait, and `errors[0].code` is `rate_limit_exceeded`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next attempt is allowed.

Gone.description: The resource existed but is no longer available, for example an expired device code.

BadGateway.description: An outbound provider (email, identity provider, SMS) refused or failed the call. The message never contains a provider credential.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A required capability is not configured on this instance, for example `email_not_configured`.

OAuthBadRequest.description: The request is malformed or an OAuth parameter is missing; `error` names the RFC 6749 code.

OAuthUnauthorized.description: Client authentication failed (`invalid_client`), or the bearer token is missing or invalid.

OrderBy.name: order_by
OrderBy.description: Sort field, prefixed with `-` for descending (`-created_at`) or `+` for ascending. An unknown field falls back to the endpoint's default order.

Paginated.name: paginated
Paginated.description: When `true`, the response is `{ data, total_count }` instead of the plain envelope.

SecretKey.description: Instance secret key (`sk_live_...` / `sk_test_...`) as `Authorization: Bearer sk_...`. Grants full Backend API access, so it must only ever be used from a server you control. The dashboard does not hold it: it exchanges it once at `POST /v1/operator_sessions` for the httpOnly `__orbit_operator` cookie, which the Backend API also accepts from this instance's own origin.

ClientCookie.name: __client
ClientCookie.description: Opaque client token set by `GET /v1/client` as an httpOnly cookie. One per browser or device.

SessionToken.description: Session JWT (RS256, 60 s lifetime) minted by `POST /v1/client/sessions/{id}/tokens`.

OAuth2.description: Access token issued by this instance's `/oauth/token` endpoint for an OAuth application.

scopes.email: Email address and whether it is verified.

scopes.machine:token: Mint tokens as a machine identity.

MachineSecret.description: Machine secret from `POST /v1/m2m/machines`. Only `/oauth/m2m/token` accepts it.
